analysis: Examined base T-047..T-058 (docs/threat-model.yaml base 1874-2260) and head 1-472. Changes visible: header comment (head 43-45) announcing TB-012, A-018, T-059 for a provider add-on hold socket; new asset A-018 provider_serving_availability (head 233-241, sensitivity medium, code ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift). TB-012 (head 811-841) and T-059 (head 2305-2337) are not in supplied units; the patch excerpt shows TB-012 describes a separately signed add-on io.darkbloom.sandbox talking over an owner-only AF_UNIX socket, same user, with machine lock coordination. This is a documentation-only change; no source code is in scope, so no concrete regression is demonstrable. Integration questions: (1) TB-012/T-059 should state that a same-user process (ADV-001 operator or any local same-user code) can impersonate the add-on unless the signature check (code-signing requirement/team ID via audit token, not PID) is robust; (2) hold should only withhold serving (availability, A-018) and never grant trust, extend authorization, or affect attestation/TB-011 grants; (3) busy fields in heartbeat are provider-origin and coordinator handling is declared platform work—ensure they are not treated as trust evidence and cannot be abused to manipulate rewards/uptime (T-055, A-009); (4) lease expiry/fallback to machine lock must fail toward serving resume or documented DoS; (5) in-flight requests on hold entry should be completed or cancelled cleanly (T-010). Need deeper review of head lines 811-841 and 2305-2337 and the AddonHold source.
